QuestionStmt.S: The frequency of a stretched uniform wire of length $L$ under tension is in resonance with the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe of same length. If the tension in the wire is increased by 8 N, it is in resonance with the first overtone of the same closed pipe. The initial tension in the wire is

Solution.S:
Fundamental frequency of a stretched wire: $f = \frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$.

Fundamental frequency of a closed pipe: $f_0 = \frac{v}{4L}$.

First overtone of closed pipe: $f_1 = \frac{3v}{4L} = 3f_0$.

Initially, wire resonates with closed pipe fundamental: $\frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \frac{v}{4L}$.

After tension increased by 8 N: $\frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\frac{T+8}{\mu}} = 3 \times \frac{v}{4L}$.

Divide the two equations:

$$\frac{\sqrt{T+8}}{\sqrt{T}} = 3 \Rightarrow \frac{T+8}{T} = 9 \Rightarrow T+8 = 9T \Rightarrow 8T = 8 \Rightarrow T = 1 \text{ N}.$$

Thus the correct option is D: 1 N.
